feedback: Iteration 0 showed the five-sensor span (x = ±0.024 m) is too narrow: line_loss_events were 1 to 2 per run and max_error reached 0.0626 m on the oval and 0.0703 m on the s-bend, so runs ended off track before any finish. To work with your seven-sensor span, I rescaled the sensor weights to x/0.018 and raised kp to 6.0, which keeps the steering gain per metre of offset equal to iteration 0. I have no race data for this candidate yet. Next race: if line_loss_events are zero but steering_oscillation rises above about 0.25 (iteration 0 range 0.13 to 0.25), the outer sensors are reacting too early, so move the forward sensor row toward y = 0.03 m, citing that iteration 0 oscillation was low enough to allow this. If line_loss_events are zero and max_error is still above 0.06 m, the limit is turn authority rather than sensing, so widen wheel_track, citing the iteration 0 max_error of 0.063 to 0.070 m. If line loss remains above zero on slalom or s-bend, keep the seven-sensor span and widen sensor_size to 0.016 m, which gives each sensor more footprint over the tape.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are zero but steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.25: move the forward sensor row from y = 0.04 m to y = 0.03 m, keeping x = ±0.036 m, since iteration 0 oscillation was 0.13 to 0.25 and the outer sensors may be reacting early.
If line_loss_events are zero but max_error stays above 0.06 m: widen wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.14 m, since iteration 0 max_error was 0.063 to 0.070 m with the sensing span the limiting factor.

If line_loss_events stay above zero on slalom or s-bend: set sensor_size to 0.016 m with the same seven x positions, so each footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape when the robot is at the edge, citing the 1 to 2 line-loss events per run in iteration 0.
